observations: Single solar panel photographed leaning against stacked white boards/panels (likely insulation or ceiling boards) in an outdoor/construction setting.
Panel has a silver/white frame and a grid of dark blue-black monocrystalline-style cells, arranged in what looks like a 6x10 layout consistent with a 60-cell format.
No manufacturer nameplate, specification sticker, serial number, or wattage label is visible or legible anywhere on the panel.
No junction box, cable, or connector is visible to assess wiring condition.
Back side of the panel (where the rating label is normally placed) is not shown.
A hand holding a phone is visible at the bottom, taking the photo; a watermark 'Nagotech Solar' and camera EXIF text overlay the image.
Surface of the panel appears clean with no visible cracks, delamination, or hot-spots from this single front angle, but lighting and resolution limit close inspection.

claims.evidence: No country-of-origin marking, import sticker, or brand label visible in photo 0.
No wattage/spec sticker visible; cell count and frame size are consistent with common 60-cell ~300-350W panels but this is not confirmed by any readable label.
Cell grid pattern in photo 0 appears consistent with a 60-cell layout, but cells are not clearly countable due to angle/resolution.

claims.claim: Used / functional ('let the sun pay the bills')
claims.evidence: No multimeter reading, output test, or sunlight test shown; only a static leaning photo is provided.

risks.proof: Clip or photo of panel connected to a multimeter/load meter under sunlight showing voltage/current output

risks.risk: Actual wattage and brand cannot be confirmed, which drives most of the price
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rear nameplate/specification sticker showing brand, model, wattage, Voc/Isc
risks.if_unproven: priced at the low end for a generic unbranded 60-cell panel of unknown wattage

risks.risk: Hidden micro-cracks, hotspots, or delamination not visible from a single front-angle photo
risks.proof: Multiple close-up photos of the full front and back surface in good light, plus an electroluminescence or shaded-cell test if available

risks.proof: Photo of the rear junction box and cable/connector close-up
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming junction box/cable may need replacement

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the rear nameplate/spec sticker (brand, model, wattage, Voc, Isc, cell count)
Photo or short video of the panel's output being measured with a multimeter under direct sunlight
Close-up photos of the rear junction box, cable, and connectors
Full-panel photos from multiple angles in good daylight showing both front and back surfaces for crack/damage inspection
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a used 60-cell style solar panel, but brand, wattage, and working condition are all unverifiable from the single photo, so it must be priced at the worst-case (generic, unverified output) level pending nameplate and performance proof.
